raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Motivation

The Rust server checks every `stop_regex` with `regex-syntax` before it reaches the scheduler, and sends the scheduler a length bound for the match window (`stop_regex_max_len`). An admitted pattern's bound must be at least CPython's max match width, or the window cannot hold a match.

`regex-syntax` accepts whitespace inside a counted repeat. It reads `a{2 }`, `a{ 2}` and `\d{1, 3}` as repeats. CPython reads them as literal text. So `\d{1, 3}` gets a bound of 3 while CPython needs 7 characters, the stop never fires, and the request runs to `max_new_tokens`. The Python server stops on the same request. A space after the comma is an easy typo to make in a hand-written stop pattern.

### Reproduction

The new corpus rows fail on current main:

```
ADMITTED but must be rejected: "a{2 }" (bound 2, worst re.search 0.01 ms)
ADMITTED but must be rejected: "a{ 2}" (bound 2, worst re.search 0.01 ms)
ADMITTED but must be rejected: "\\d{1, 3}" (bound 3, worst re.search 0.01 ms)
```

Effect on the scheduler. This drives the real `Req._check_str_based_finish` with a tokenizer that emits one character per token, fed one token at a time as decode does.

```
pattern='\\d{1, 3}' text='The answer is 5{1, 3} and then more text follows here.'
  python bound 7: fires=True  (FINISHED_MATCHED_REGEX)
  rust   bound 3: fires=False
```

## Modifications

- `spaced_repetition_operator` rejects a repetition operator whose source text holds whitespace. The request gets a 400. The check only rejects, so the bound of every pattern still admitted is unchanged. Spacing outside a repeat, such as `a {2}` and `[ ]{2}`, stays admitted.
- A new unit test runs CPython's `re` on every pattern the tests expect Rust to admit. It checks that each one compiles and that the Rust bound is at least CPython's `sre_parse` max width. It is skipped when no `python3` can be started (`PYTHON` overrides the interpreter).

## Tests

- 3 `MustReject` corpus rows, with `py_max_len` from SGLang's `get_max_seq_length` and `worst_ms` from timed `re.search` runs.
- `whitespace_outside_a_repeat_operator_is_still_admitted` guards against over-rejection.
- `admitted_patterns_compile_in_cpython_within_their_bound` passes. With the new check disabled it fails with `"\\d{1, 3}" rust bound 3 < CPython max width 7`.
- `cargo test -p sglang-server --lib utils::regex`: 14 passed.
- `cargo fmt -p sglang-server --check` and `cargo clippy -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` are clean.

## Accuracy Tests

Model forward code is unchanged. Only `stop_regex` admission changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Not applicable. The change touches request validation only.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

nodes.body:
@rainj-me @merrymercy could one of you comment `/tag-and-rerun-ci` here? The current red checks are the `run-ci` label gate, so no build or test has run yet.

I ran the sglang-server checks locally on this branch (6eede477):

- `cargo fmt -p sglang-server --check` passes
- `cargo clippy --locked -p sglang-server --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes
- `cargo test --locked -p sglang-server` gives 382 passed. The 13 failures are shared memory tests that hit `shm_open: Permission denied` in my sandbox. The same 13 fail on unmodified main (c5e734e4, 381 passed), and the extra pass is the new `whitespace_outside_a_repeat_operator_is_still_admitted` test.

Thanks!

@rainj-me could you trigger CI for this one with `/tag-and-rerun-ci` when you have a moment? It only touches `rust/sglang-server/src/utils/regex.rs`.

The Rust server admits five `stop_regex` shapes that CPython reads differently (found by a differential fuzzer against CPython 3.11 and 3.12), which breaks the module's contract that anything Rust admits, Python can compile with at least the same match-window bound. The fix rejects those shapes at admission. `Check PR title` passes; CI is waiting on the `run-ci` label. Thanks!

@rainj-me Thanks, agreed. I narrowed the PR to the one case a user is likely to hit: whitespace inside a repeat count such as `\d{1, 3}`. Rust reads it as a repeat with bound 3 and CPython reads it as literal text that needs 7 characters, so the stop silently never fires. The `(?x)`, group-name, `~~` and `\x 41` rules are gone.

I also added `admitted_patterns_compile_in_cpython_within_their_bound`. It runs CPython's `re` on every pattern the tests expect Rust to admit, and checks that each one compiles and that the Rust bound covers CPython's max width. It skips when `python3` is unavailable. With the new check turned off it fails on `\d{1, 3}`.

@rainj-me thanks for the approval! All required checks are green on `363ebbde90` (`lint`, `Check PR title`, `pr-test-finish`). The remaining red ones are the optional Extra tiers, which wait for the `run-ci-extra` label. It is ready to merge whenever convenient.

The cpython regex support way more rules than rust regex. We should only add the rules that actually in used instead of mimic all the corner cases within cpython re lib.  The major gaps are backreferences and lookaround.

Meanwhile some rules that rust regex tolerance  that python re lib will break, so better add re validation within the unit tests if possible.
